question:
The radius of a spherical object is measured as $10\ \text{cm}$ with a possible error of $0.02\ \text{cm}$. Using differentials, determine:

(a) the maximum approximate error in its calculated volume;

(b) the corresponding percentage error in its volume;

(c) the maximum approximate error and percentage error in its surface area.
explanation:
(a)
The volume of a sphere is
$$V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$$
Differentiating,
$$dV=4\pi r^2\,dr$$
For $r=10\ \text{cm}$ and $|dr|=0.02\ \text{cm}$,
$$|dV|=4\pi(10)^2(0.02)$$
$$|dV|=8\pi\ \text{cm}^3$$
Thus, the maximum approximate error in the volume is $8\pi\ \text{cm}^3$.

(b)
The relative error in volume is
$$\frac{|dV|}{V}=3\frac{|dr|}{r}$$
Therefore, the percentage error is
$$3\times\frac{0.02}{10}\times 100=0.6\%$$

(c)
The surface area of a sphere is
$$S=4\pi r^2$$
Differentiating,
$$dS=8\pi r\,dr$$
Therefore,
$$|dS|=8\pi(10)(0.02)=1.6\pi\ \text{cm}^2$$
The relative error in surface area is
$$\frac{|dS|}{S}=2\frac{|dr|}{r}$$
Hence, the percentage error is
$$2\times\frac{0.02}{10}\times 100=0.4\%$$
Thus, the maximum approximate error in surface area is $1.6\pi\ \text{cm}^2$, and its percentage error is $0.4\%$.

(c) Surface-area error $0.8\pi$ cm$^2$ and percentage error $0.2\%$
